from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Cones are surfaces formed by rotation.", "Slicing cones creates conic sections.", "Circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas emerge."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Slicing Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/2, axis=RIGHT)
        label_cone = Text("Cone", font_size=24, color=WHITE)

        intersection = Circle(radius=0.7, color=PURPLE, stroke_width=4)
        label_inter = Text("Intersection", font_size=24, color=PURPLE)

        # Positioning
        self.place_in_area(cone, "A2", "C5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(label_cone, "A2")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(cone), Write(label_cone))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.place_in_area(intersection, "C3", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(intersection), Write(label_inter), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(cone.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=OUT), intersection.animate.rotate(PI/6, axis=OUT), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Universal Application", ["This holds for all conics.", "Parabolas use one sphere tangency.", "Hyperbolas use two spheres tangency."])
        
        # Parabola Visualization (Placeholder geometries for representation)
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT)
        sphere1 = Sphere(radius=0.4).set_color(BLUE)
        parabola_curve = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5*t**2, 0]), t_range=[-1, 1])
        
        parabola_group = VGroup(cone, sphere1, parabola_curve).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(parabola_group, 'B2')
        
        # Hyperbola Visualization
        cone2 = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2).rotate(PI/4, axis=RIGHT)
        sphere2 = Sphere(radius=0.3).set_color(RED)
        sphere3 = Sphere(radius=0.3).set_color(RED).shift(DOWN*0.5)
        hyperbola_curve = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([t, np.sqrt(1+t**2), 0]), t_range=[-1, 1])
        
        hyperbola_group = VGroup(cone2, sphere2, sphere3, hyperbola_curve).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_group, 'E2')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(parabola_group), Create(hyperbola_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(sphere1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(sphere2), Indicate(sphere3))
        
        # Final Highlight
        self.play(parabola_group.animate.set_color("#00CCFF"), hyperbola_group.animate.set_color("#00CCFF"))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", ["Conics are 3D geometric results.", "Spheres link visuals to algebra.", "Dandelin spheres unify conic properties."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show all three conic types appearing from slices. Color: #FFFFFF.
        c1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        c2 = Ellipse(width=1.0, height=0.6, color=WHITE).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.3)
        c3 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[-1, 1], color=WHITE).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3).scale(0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(c2, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(c3, 'B6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(c1), FadeIn(c2), FadeIn(c3))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the common Dandelin sphere principle. Color: #FFFF00.
        sphere1 = Sphere(radius=0.3, color=YELLOW).set_opacity(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(sphere1, 'D3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere1))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade all elements into a unified diagram. Color: #FFFFFF.
        group = VGroup(c1, c2, c3, sphere1)
        self.play(group.animate.move_to(self.grid['E4']), FadeOut(c1), FadeOut(c2), FadeOut(c3))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unlocking the Geometry of Cones: Dandelin Spheres
outline.target_audience: High school geometry students or early undergraduate math enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction: The Slicing Problem
sections.content: Define the cone and the plane intersection. Briefly review prerequisite knowledge: A cone is a surface formed by rotating a line around an axis. When we slice it, we get conic sections (circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas).
sections.example: Imagine slicing a carrot with a knife at different angles to create different cross-sections.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Visual setup: Introduce two imaginary spheres inscribed inside the cone, tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the slicing plane (at a point). This is the 'Aha!' moment where 3D geometry explains 2D shapes.
sections.example: Visualize two floating bubbles inside a party hat, touching the 'slice' paper at specific points (foci).

sections.title: The Ellipse Connection
sections.content: Show how the distances from any point on the intersection ellipse to the two contact points of the spheres sum up to a constant (the distance between the two circles of tangency). This bridges the gap between 'slicing' and the algebraic definition of an ellipse.
sections.example: A 'pinball' animation where a ball bounces between the two sphere contact points, maintaining a constant path length.

sections.title: Universal Application
sections.content: Briefly demonstrate that this principle holds for parabolas and hyperbolas (using one or two spheres). Explain why this is important: it proves that the geometric 'foci' of conics are not just abstract points, but physical contact points of spheres.
sections.example: A satellite dish (parabolic) receiving signals that all converge to the 'sphere contact point' (the focus).

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Conic sections aren't just equations; they are the natural result of 3D geometry. Dandelin spheres unify the visual 'slice' with the algebraic 'focus-directrix' properties.
sections.example: An animation morphing a circular slice into an elliptical one, showing the spheres growing and shifting to accommodate the change.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The 'Intersection' label overlaps with the cone graphic, obscuring visual clarity. Fix: Line 67: self.place_at_grid(intersection, 'D3', scale_factor=0.7) (line=67, object=intersection)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The cone graphic placement (A2-C5) is too close to the left, crowding the lecture text area. Fix: Line 58: self.place_in_area(cone, 'B3', 'E6', scale_factor=1.2) (line=58, object=cone)

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The label 'Cone' is visually detached from the object due to its high placement at A2. Fix: Line 59: self.place_at_grid(label_cone, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8) (line=59, object=label_cone)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Current grid occupancy (B2-D4, C1-E5, C3-D4) causes significant visual overlap and clustering, cluttering the center-right view. Fix: Line 74: self.place_in_area(contact_circles, 'B2', 'C3', scale_factor=0.6) (line=74, object=contact_circles)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The slicing plane is placed too low (C1-E5), encroaching on the lower grid rows and creating potential off-screen clipping at the bottom. Fix: Line 81: self.place_in_area(plane, 'B4', 'D6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=81, object=plane)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The foci points are obscured by the overlapping plane and sphere elements due to excessive centralized placement in C3-D4. Fix: Line 88: self.place_at_grid(foci, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5) (line=88, object=foci)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The ellipse occupies a wide area (A1-C4) and is positioned too far to the left, crowding the lecture notes and risking overlap. Fix: Line 62: self.place_in_area(ellipse, 'B3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=62, object=ellipse)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The focal point labels (B2, B4) are centered inside the ellipse region, causing potential visual clutter with the ellipse boundary. Fix: Line 63: self.place_at_grid(focus1, 'C3', scale_factor=0.6); Line 64: self.place_at_grid(focus2, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=63, object=focus1 and focus2)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Focal and Sum labels are placed too low (D3, E3), creating a disjointed layout that ignores the right-side grid symmetry. Fix: Line 69: self.place_at_grid(focal_label, 'D4', scale_factor=0.7); Line 70: self.place_at_grid(sum_label, 'E4', scale_factor=0.7) (line=69, object=focal_label and sum_label)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The animations are centered too far to the left, causing them to conflict with the lecture text area. Fix: Line 56: self.place_at_grid(parabola_group, 'B5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=56, object=parabola_group)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The hyperbola animation position at E2 is too close to the vertical axis of the text area. Fix: Line 65: self.place_at_grid(hyperbola_group, 'E5', scale_factor=0.6) (line=65, object=hyperbola_group)

[VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Poor vertical distribution; the two groups are clustered in the top-left quadrant of the grid area, leaving the right side unused. Fix: self.place_in_area(parabola_group, 'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_in_area(hyperbola_group, 'D4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=56, object=both_groups)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: Dandelin sphere animation (sphere1) obstructs the viewing area as it is positioned too low and potentially interferes with future content space. Fix: Line 65: self.place_at_grid(sphere1, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6) (line=65, object=sphere1)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The conic objects (c1, c2, c3) are tightly clustered in row B, creating a cramped layout that does not balance well with the left-aligned text. Fix: Line 55: self.place_at_grid(c1, 'B2', scale_factor=0.7); Line 56: self.place_at_grid(c2, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7); Line 57: self.place_at_grid(c3, 'B6', scale_factor=0.7) (line=55, object=c1, c2, c3)

[VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The current scaling of the conic objects (default) is too large, competing with the text for visual hierarchy. Fix: Line 55-57: Adjusted scale_factor to 0.7 for all objects to maintain clear separation from the title area. (line=55, object=c1, c2, c3)

Fix visual layout issues: Current grid occupancy (B2-D4, C1-E5, C3-D4) causes clustering. Move contact_circles to B2-C3 (scale 0.6). Move plane to B4-D6 (scale 0.7). Move foci to E4 (scale 0.5).

Fix visual layout issues: The ellipse occupies A1-C4 and is too far left; move to B3-E5 (scale 0.6). Focal points are cluttered inside ellipse; move focus1 to C3, focus2 to C5 (scale 0.6). Move focal_label to D4 and sum_label to E4 (scale 0.7).

Fix visual layout issues: Animations are too far left; move parabola_group to B5 (scale 0.6) and hyperbola_group to E5 (scale 0.6). Improve vertical distribution by moving both to area A4-C6 (parabola) and D4-F6 (hyperbola) with scale 0.7.
Fix visual layout issues: Move sphere1 to E3 (scale 0.6). Realign conics c1, c2, c3: move c1 to B2, c2 to B4, c3 to B6 (all scale 0.7).
